title: Zero test characterization
statement: Let $D$ be an algebraic circuit on $n$ inputs, and let $r$ be a finite bit string. Its zero-test on $r$ is true exactly when, for every integer $j$ with $0 \le j < 8(\operatorname{size}(D)+12)$, evaluating $D$ at the point whose $i$th coordinate is one plus the integer encoded by the $(\operatorname{size}(D)+4)$-bit block of $r$ beginning at position $i(\operatorname{size}(D)+4)$, with arithmetic in the residue ring modulo one plus the integer encoded by the $2(\operatorname{size}(D)+12)$-bit block of $r$ beginning after its first $n(\operatorname{size}(D)+4)$ bits and then at offset $j\,2(\operatorname{size}(D)+12)$, gives zero.
